newsitem.title: UK: UK's ONS says no inquiry into RPI accuracy.
newsitem.headline: UK's ONS says no inquiry into RPI accuracy.

text.p: Britain's Office for National Statistics said on Friday it had no plans to look into potential bias in its retail price inflation index.

Channel 4 news reported on Thursday that the ONS had launched an inquiry into the accuracy of inflation figures, adding that the government was concerned about the current series overstating the real level of inflation.
"There is no formal enquiry into potential bias in the RPI as raised by Channel 4," an ONS spokesman said. "The ONS did not say that."

"However, we will continue to carry out our usual research and development of the figures to ensure that the RPI remains the most accurate measure of inflation as experienced by the vast majority of households in the UK."

Retail price data published on Thursday showed underlying inflation stuck at 3.1 percent year-on-year in January, well above the government's target of 2.5 percent. The spokesman said the ONS was aware of concerns raised in the United States about the validity of inflation measures but was confident that any U.S. problems were not applicable to the UK RPI.

Two weeks ago, the U.S. Senate Finance Committee introduced a resolution to test the accuracy of the consumer price index. An advisory commission reported in December that the CPI overstated the cost of living by 1.1 percentage points.

The ONS spokesman said: "We will be going through our normal, annual updating of the basket of goods and services used to keep track of inflation. But, there are no plans to change our methods of calculation."
About 600 goods and services are monitored in the ONS basket for RPI.
